stories.title: Day Highlights: New Zealand vs India, Day 1 | 2nd Test
stories.summary: Akash Deep emerged as India's standout bowler on the opening day of the second Test against New Zealand, producing two outstanding deliveries in the post-lunch session to overshadow even the impressive Jasprit Bumrah. After winning the toss and electing to bowl, India initially struggled to make inroads as New Zealand captain Tom Latham and Devon Conway put together a 77-run opening partnership.

stories.title: India A knocked out of Asia Cup Rising Stars after loss to Sri Lanka A in semis
stories.summary: A spirited Sri Lanka A rode on centuries from openers Lasith Croospulle (116) and Sineth Jayawardene (105) to decimate a star-studded India A by eight wickets and reach the Asia Cup Rising Stars final here on Thursday. Both Croospulle and Jayawardene received early reprieves in the form of dropped catches and made India A, which had several international cricketers at its disposal, rue those mistakes.

stories.title: Litchfield stars as Thunder beat Strikers in record run-fest
stories.summary: Litchfield made 121 not out as Thunder held on against Strikers in WBBL record 473-run thriller at North Sydney Oval

stories.title: India's Pant joins New Zealand club match under false name
stories.summary: India wicketkeeper Rishabh Pant made a surprise appearance for a club team in Christchurch under the false name 'Stan Stan'. Pant, 29, played for the Open House Swingers against The Chosen Ones and smashed 54 from 21 balls in a 16-run win. His appearance came a day before India's second Test against New Zealand, which begins at the Hagley Oval at 22:00 GMT on Thursday.

stories.title: Was Siraj crying after 2nd Test snub? Ex-India spinner wonders on live TV
stories.summary: Siraj was dropped for the first Test in Wellington last week, with India opting for Jasprit Bumrah, Akash Deep, Anshul Kamboj and Prasidh Krishna in their pace attack. The match ended in a draw after India's bowlers failed to take all 20 New Zealand wickets. There was no place for Siraj in Christchurch either.

stories.title: India win toss, elect to field in second Test against New Zealand
stories.summary: India captain Shubman Gill won the toss and elected to field in the second and final test against New Zealand in Christchurch on Friday. India made one change to their starting XI from the drawn first test in Wellington, bringing in fast bowler Gurnoor Brar for Prasidh Krishna on a grassy pitch at Hagley Oval.

stories.title: What happens now for Bayern Munich and Musiala?
stories.summary: Bayern Munich - and representatives of one of their most prominent players -have collided over recent weeks. During the summer, the public became aware that their star 23-year-old midfielder Jamal Musiala suffered from absence seizures. This neurological condition causes a brief, sudden lapse in awareness and responsiveness. Musiala had two of these lapses during pre-season games, but episodes already happened during the previous year.

stories.title: 'Carefree' Shami content to focus on white-ball cricket after Test retirement
stories.summary: The 36-year-old, whose last international appearance came in the Champions Trophy in 2025, said he was happy to leave selection decisions to the selectors and wanted to enjoy whatever cricket he had left in him. Asked if the 2027 ODI World Cup or the 2028 T20 World Cup featured in his plans, Shami said he was no longer looking that far ahead.

stories.title: 2036 Olympics bid: India to make presentation to IOC
stories.summary: Union sports minister Mansukh Mandaviya and outgoing Indian Olympic Association (IOA) president PT Usha will head the country’s delegation that will discuss India's 2036 Olympic bid with officials of the International Olympic Committee (IOC) on Thursday.

stories.title: India presents 2036 Olympic vision to IOC Future Host Commission in virtual meeting
stories.summary: The Indian delegation was led by Indian Olympic Association (IOA) president PT Usha, CEO Raghuram Iyer and IOA Athletes’ Commission chairperson PV Sindhu. Ahmedabad is at the centre of India’s proposed hosting model, with the city set to host the 2030 Commonwealth Games. The presentation highlighted Ahmedabad’s infrastructure readiness and the support extended by city, state and central authorities.

stories.title: 'I want us to go all the way': PV Sindhu eyes historic Uber Cup triumph as India gets 2028 hosting rights
stories.summary: Sindhu was part of the Indian women's squad that created history by securing the country's first-ever Uber Cup medal, a bronze, when New Delhi hosted the tournament in 2014. "I was proud of the bronze we won in Delhi in 2014. If I get another chance to play the Uber Cup at home, I want us to go all the way.

stories.title: Tamil Nadu’s SMAT campaign exposes reluctance to move beyond familiar personnel and approaches
stories.summary: The most successful team in the competition with three titles, Tamil Nadu has endured its fifth successive group-stage exit in the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy (SMAT) this season. It won three of its seven matches and finished sixth among eight teams in Group B. The campaign exposed a reluctance to move beyond familiar personnel and approaches, even as modern T20 cricket demands greater intent, flexibility and tactical imagination.

stories.title: Familiar faces and surprise chances as Ireland face Wallabies
stories.summary: Discussion about how Ireland head coach Andy Farrell would approach Friday's Nations Championship fifth-place play-off against Australia was ended emphatically by the team announcement on Wednesday. While Farrell would have been excused for fielding a rotated side in the wake of last week's bruising victory over world champions South Africa , he instead opted for continuity and is challenging his first-choice line-up to produce another chest-thumping 80-minute display against the Wallabies.

stories.title: Yashasvi Jaiswal surpasses Sachin Tendulkar to create history with rare Test feat
stories.summary: The India opener reached the landmark during the second Test against New Zealand at Hagley Oval in Christchurch. Former India batter Sanjay Manjrekar is the only other player to have achieved the feat, having played his first 33 Tests at 33 different venues. Former India fast bowler Javagal Srinath and West Indies wicketkeeper-batter Denesh Ramdin complete the top five.

stories.title: Standing up to 140kph: How keepers are turning an old tactic into an attacking weapon
stories.summary: Former India wicketkeeper Chandrakant Pandit believes it is a response to how batting has evolved in the post-T20 era. “Today’s batters, even in Tests, have the courage to step out against pace. ”There is evidence that it works. Henry explained why the Kiwis did it at the Basin for a long period of time.

stories.title: New Zealand nose ahead of India after Day 1 in Christchurch
stories.summary: Christchurch, the main metropolis in the South Island of New Zealand, is a most English city. Even the river flowing through it is called Avon, like the one with the same name in southwest England. It is aptly described as a garden city. At the heart of this urban centre is a vast expanse of greenery, including a botanical garden.

stories.title: Hasn’t looked dangerous with second new ball: Sunil Gavaskar highlights Jasprit Bumrah's lack of zip
stories.summary: Former India captain Sunil Gavaskar expressed a word of caution regarding Jasprit Bumrah , saying the pacer didn't look threatening with the second new ball on Day 1 of the second Test at Christchurch on Friday. The 32-year-old's pace was relatively down in the final session at the Hagley Oval, with speeds hovering in the 127-130 kmph range.

stories.title: Why is Jasprit Bumrah using a different run-up? Akash Deep has an answer
stories.summary: Jasprit Bumrah exhibited a different run-up style during the second Test match against New Zealand in Christchurch. While he did not take any wickets on the opening day, other Indian bowlers made significant contributions. Akash Deep was particularly effective, taking two crucial wickets to help India gain momentum.

stories.title: Akash Deep sizzles, Jasprit Bumrah struggles as NZ frustrate India on Day 1
stories.summary: Akash Deep's incisive spell triggered a three-wicket collapse in 22 balls to put India back in the contest, but Tom Blundell and Glenn Phillips steadied New Zealand with an unbeaten stand. Jasprit Bumrah's wicketless, unusually subdued spell, meanwhile, raised questions despite India's fightback.

stories.title: Glenn makes 'free ball' history in WBBL after Dottin timed out
stories.summary: Watch the moment England's Sarah Glenn makes history in the women's Big Bash League as she bowls at an empty set of stumps with a 'free ball', to dismiss Deandra Dottin after the batter was ruled to have taken too long to face the delivery.

stories.title: Do Indian bodies burn calories differently? Country’s 1st advanced metabolic chamber seeks answers
stories.summary: The Human Metabolic Chamber at Vellore’s Christian Medical College (CMC) was jointly established by the college and the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research’s (TIFR) Advanced Research Unit on Metabolism, Development and Aging (ARUMDA) and is designed to give researchers a more precise picture of how the human body burns calories and uses different sources of energy.

stories.title: When will Poundland shops close? Five key questions answered
stories.summary: Poundland has collapsed into administration, leaving the jobs of its 11,000 staff in doubt in the run-up to Christmas. The company has appointed consultancy Alix Partners to oversee a sale of part or all of the discount retailer, with questions remaining about the future of the company. Poundland collapsing has acted as a reset of the process of selling the company.

stories.title: Mint explainer: why HPV vaccination is critical for girls as India crosses 10 million doses
stories.summary: India has administered more than 10 million doses of the human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine to 14-year-old girls in less than nine months under a campaign by the Union health ministry. The drive has covered nearly 87% of the annual target cohort of about 12 million girls, drawing praise from the World Health Organization’s (WHO) South-East Asia Region.

stories.title: Explained: What is ‘Starmind’? SpaceX gets FCC nod for 1 million space-based data centres - Full details
stories.summary: SpaceX has received approval from the US Federal Communications Commission (FCC) to deploy up to 1 million orbital computing modules for a proposed constellation of space-based data centres, marking a major push to take artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure beyond Earth.

stories.title: Explainer-Spain’s snap election — why it matters and who might win?
stories.summary: MADRID, Nov 26 (Reuters) – Spain goes to the polls on Sunday in an early parliamentary election that may usher in a right-wing coalition to replace the Socialist-led minority government of Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez, one of Europe’s last leftist leaders. Sanchez called the election after parliament on October 2 rejected his decrees to address growing anger over rising rents and evictions.

stories.title: Who Is Vardhaman Jain? Chennai Businessman Offers 121 Kg Gold Ornaments Worth ₹206 Cr To Lord Venkateswara
stories.summary: Chennai-based industrialist and philanthropist Vardhaman Jain has made a significant religious contribution by donating 121 kg of gold ornaments valued at ₹160 crore to the Tirumala Temple in Andhra Pradesh. Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu visited the temple on Thursday, Nov 26, to attend the formal handover ceremony.

stories.title: Can India’s Capital Markets Unlock The Viksit Bharat Dream? ICRA-ASSOCHAM Outlines Roadmap For Financial Growth
stories.summary: Mumbai: India’s capital markets are expected to play a pivotal role in financing the country’s transition towards a developed economy by 2047, with greater market depth, liquidity and institutional participation emerging as critical priorities, according to an ICRA-ASSOCHAM report released on Friday. The report highlighted the need for a more inclusive financial ecosystem capable of mobilising long-term investments and supporting sustainable economic growth .

stories.title: Knowledge Nugget | EPFO’s new rules explained: From easier PF withdrawals to payout plan for retirees
stories.summary: The Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO), at the meeting of its Central Board of Trustees (CBT) on November 19, 2026, approved key changes to Provident Fund (PF) withdrawal rules. These include reducing the waiting period for final PF settlement after unemployment from 12 months to two months, lowering the minimum balance that members must retain in their accounts from 25% to 10%, and introducing a Systematic Withdrawal Plan (SWP).

stories.title: Everyday Explained: Why sparkling water fizzes more on first pour and then quickly goes flat
stories.summary: From bubbles to flat water, here are the reasons why sparkling water loses its fizz after pouring it into a glass. Sparkling water gets its characteristic fizz from dissolved carbon dioxide, which creates bubbles when the bottle is opened and the pressure changes. However, the moment you pour it into a glass, the drink begins to lose some of that carbonation.

stories.title: Diljit Dosanjh's Mumbai concert today: 500+ cops, bomb squads and no-car zone after threat email; MNS seeks ban on racecourse shows over drugs
stories.summary: Diljit Dosanjh's concert at Mumbai's Mahalaxmi Racecourse on Friday, part of his RuPay AURA India Tour 2026, is under heightened security after a threat email. More than 500 police personnel, bomb detection teams and a no-car zone are in place. Meanwhile, the MNS has demanded a ban on concerts at the venue, alleging drug use and disruption.

stories.title: Rs 11-lakh Chandelier, Rs 6-lakh Temple: Inside Kejriwal’s Former ‘Sheesh Mahal’, Soon To Open To Public
stories.summary: After remaining the BJP's key criticism of the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) and its common man-friendly image, former Delhi chief minister Arvind Kejriwal's erstwhile official residence was opened for a media tour on Friday. Dubbed the 'Sheesh Mahal', the Kejriwal's former Flagstaff Road bungalow was used as ammunition by the BJP ahead of the Delhi Assembly election last year.
